text:
maria: seeing a ~18% p99 latency regression on main after yesterday's compiler toggles. only on fp8 path and only for long-seq chat workloads.
kevin: which toggle exactly? Triton or CUTLASS?
maria: TURNED_ON: triton_fusion=1, cutlass_fastpath=auto, nvcc_arch_probe=dynamic. reverted cutlass_fastpath to off and perf went back.
ashok: can you paste profiler traces? sounds like kernel selection flapped between two variants.
maria: paste from trace: 
```
[TRACE] layer 42 choose kernel: cutlass_fp8_gemm_fast (lat 0.42ms)
[TRACE] layer 42 choose kernel: triton_fp8_gemm_generic (lat 0.95ms)
[TRACE] kvcache miss rate spike at seq>1024 -> batching changed -> chosen kernel flips mid-run
```
kevin: aha. the runtime picks kernel based on shape + arch probe score. if batch/sz distribution shifts it can flip to fallback kernel with worse perf.
denise: does calibration affect selection? we shipped a new calib profile for fp8 last week. could quant scales push path to different kernel?
maria: possibly — we saw slightly different scale ranges with that calib. also noticed the linker path produced different CUTLASS symbol mangles when built with -O3 vs -Ofast. not sure if that matters.
kevin: action plan: 1) reproduce with deterministic batch shapes and KV warmup off 2) run microbench with both builds 3) collect per-kernel counts and sm version mapping.
maria: repro script added: 
```bash
# repro loop
python tools/repro_longseq.py --model redwood-mix-small --seq 1600 --batch-dist skewed --kv-warmup 0 
# build variants
./build.sh --triton-toggle=on --cutlass-fastpath=on --nvcc-probe=dynamic
./build.sh --triton-toggle=on --cutlass-fastpath=off --nvcc-probe=dynamic
```
ashok: I ran microbench on A100 sm80 and SM90 dev node. with cutlass_fastpath=on we get 17% higher tokens/s for short seq but regress on long seq. looks like fastpath expects contiguous KV layout; when KV cache misses and we do fragmented merges, cutlass_fastpath kernel stalls.
kevin: can bench-bot dump shape histograms per request? @bench-bot any stats?
bench-bot: shape_hist: [1..512]: 68%, [513..1024]: 22%, [1025..2048]: 10%. kv_miss_by_seq: seq>1024 -> 3.8x miss rate. avg_batch_switches_per_sec: 12.
maria: thanks. hypothesis: fastpath kernel soft-fails when batch has mixed kv-hot/kv-cold entries; runtime then picks triton generic which is slower. combined with extra synchronization overhead yields p99 hit.
denise: workaround options: - pin cutlass_fastpath=off for long-seq workloads - add an arch flag that forces kernel pruning by seq len - or make the kernel selection cost model include kv-miss penalty.
kevin: long term: update calibration to include kv-warmup scenarios so selection uses realistic perf numbers. short term: add heuristic: if fraction(seq>1024) > 0.1 then prefer fallback-stable kernel to avoid flips.
maria: I'll add the heuristic PR. also adding telemetry: per-request chosen_kernel + kv_miss_fraction so we can correlate in dashboards.
ashok: small ask: when you flame the PR, add a toggle guard so Dedicated customers can opt-in. keep default conservative.
maria: yep. will do. filing follow-up ticket: INF-7284.
kevin: thx. if anyone sees similar regressions on INT8 or 4-bit, ping here. suspect same root cause. :eyes:
denise: FYI I'm scheduling a cutlass rebuild with strict symbol visibility to make kernel identity deterministic across builds. might help reproducibility.
maria: closing loop once PR is in and we have perf numbers. cheers :rocket:
